{{Quote|Are you sure this is the Delrakkin system?''"<br />"''What were you expecting? Maybe a giant sign that says THIS WAY TO DELRAKKIN?|Leia Organa and Han Solo|<ref name="m3" />}}
'''Delrakkin''' was the only [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Delrakkin system/Legends|Delrakkin system]] capable of sustaining life. Home to the reptilian [[Delrakkin (species)/Legends|Delrakkin]], the world was covered with [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] ranges and [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]], as well as a perpetual [[Cloud/Legends|cloud]] cover that provided it with incessant storms and [[Water/Legends|rain]]. [[Delrakkin City]] was the only civilized location on the planet and was home to the Delrakkin, until the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] invaded.

The Imperials expelled the Delrakkin from their city and populated it with their own citizens. In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the planet nearly became the subject of an Imperial experiment devised by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Tarkin planned to use the planet as a test bed for new [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdictor]] technology, which was to be developed in the utmost secrecy. To that end, [[Gender/Legends|he]] ordered [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Termo]] to [[Battle against Liquidator|eradicate]] the planet's populace, providing at least two plots, one of which would have the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] framed for the act. This was not to be, however, as the scheme was foiled by the evacuation of the intended [[Death/Legends|targets]] organized by the Rebellion.

==Description==
{{Quote|Spacers say that Delrakkin's greatest natural resource is its bad weather.|Han Solo|<ref name="m3" />}}
The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Delrakkin was located within the [[Delrakkin system/Legends|Delrakkin system]], which was at the end of a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] that led to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It shared the [[Star system/Legends|system]] with two other planets, but was the only one to sustain life.<ref name="m3" />

Apart from Delrakkin's constant storms, its climate was very similar to that of [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]]. The tumultuous weather was referred to as Delrakkin's greatest natural resource by some, and it was so dangerous that most of the planet's [[Delrakkin (species)/Legends|natives]] lived underground. The storms caused perpetual, unrelenting rain on the planet. The only place considered civilized was [[Delrakkin City]], which was situated on a high [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]], above the clouds and storms. In addition to the mountain that was home to Delrakkin City, the planet featured several other vast ranges, pockmarked with caves, which were occasionally used for shelter by the natives. Apart from its mountains, Delrakkin was covered with large jungles.<ref name="m3" />

==History==
Delrakkin was considered a good place to hide by [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], until the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] invaded, forcing the Delrakkin out of Delrakkin City. The Imperials tolerated the native presence, on the condition that they not enter their city. Instead, Delrakkin City was populated by Imperial citizens.<ref name="m3" /> During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], groups of [[Stenax]] immigrated to Delrakkin after their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Stenos/Legends|Stenos]] was also invaded by the Empire. The purpose of the Stenax on Delrakkin was to survey whether or not the planet was a candidate for conquest, as they were doing simultaneously on worlds such as [[Kabray]], [[Cilpar]], and [[Keyorin]]. To make the most out of their reconnaissance, the Stenax also examined the technology of the Delrakkins.<ref name="ms" />

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Delrakkin became the target of a scheme initiated by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. It was Tarkin's plan to use Delrakkin as a testing bed for new [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdictor]] technology, which could be used to pull [[Starship/Legends|ships]] from and prevent them from reentering [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Delrakkin was chosen due to its location at the end of a hyperlane. Since the development was to be top secret, [[Gender/Legends|he]] ordered his subordinate, [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Termo]] of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Liquidator (Imperial II-class)|''Liquidator'']], to maintain a presence in the system, until the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] arrived. The [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] was carrying a shipment of poisoned [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] large enough to facilitate the extermination of the whole populace, which would be supplied to Delrakkin City's medical centers. Within days, the populace would be eradicated, allowing Tarkin to operate in secrecy.<ref name="m3" />

However, the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] did not arrive due to its [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] at [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], leaving Termo to pursue Tarkin's secondary plan. [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Skeezer]], one of Tarkin's agents, had disguised himself as a Rebel and, with the aid of the natives, had planted [[Alazhi/Legends|alazhi]], a vital ingredient in the production of bacta, on the planet, claiming that the Alliance was attempting to create their own bacta supplies on Delrakkin. The natives had believed Skeezer, making Termo's work easier. He ordered his [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to attack Delrakkin City, asserting that the citizens had consorted with the Alliance and had been planting alazhi without authorization. Providing his unwitting troops with Alliance starships, he hoped to have Delrakkin City totally razed, with any survivors pinning the massacre on the Rebels themselves.<ref name="m3" />

The [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], flown by Alliance sympathizers [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], arrived in the Delrakkin system during the faux Rebel [[Battle against Liquidator|attack]]. Its passengers, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], and [[Q-7N]], were all members of the Alliance, and together, the group decided to save Delrakkin's inhabitants from disaster, and the Alliance from public shame. Utilizing a [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]] and the aid of native Delrakkin [[Untrilla]] and [[Gwann]], the Imperial attack was fought off, and the ''Liquidator'' driven out of the system, forcing the Imperials to look elsewhere for testing grounds.<ref name="m3" />

==Inhabitants==
Delrakkin was populated by a reptilian, green-skinned [[Species/Legends|species]] of the same name. Their culture was a violent one, with trust established through tests of one-on-one combat. Following their eviction from Delrakkin City by the Empire, the planet's natives chose to live underground, keeping themselves safe from the planet's constantly violent weather. Immigrants lived in Delrakkin City, far away from the natives atop a high mountain. The Imperials kept a [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] of troops and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] on the planet, to maintain the peace and ward off any unwelcome intruders.<ref name="m3" />

==Locations==
{{Main|Delrakkin City}}
[[File:DelrakkinMap.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A map of Delrakkin City and its surroundings.]]
Delrakkin City was situated atop a tall mountain, above the planet's stormy cloud cover. Built by the Delrakkin, the planet was home to Imperial citizens following the Galactic Empire's invasion of the planet. As a line of defense, a large [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] was installed in the side of the mountain. A large tower supplied the settlement with power, although its destruction would potentially spell doom for the entire populace. The city was made up of towering skyscrapers which were severely damaged in a faux Alliance attack on the city by the Imperials in 0 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]]. Just south of the city was the [[Stiegan Jungle]].<ref name="m3" />

==Behind the scenes==
Delrakkin first appeared in [[Ryder Windham]]'s role-playing novel ''[[Star Wars Missions 1: Assault on Yavin Four]]'', published in [[1997]].<ref name="m1">''[[Star Wars Missions 1: Assault on Yavin Four]]''</ref>
